title: They Have Played Four ODIs in Eight Years. On Saturday, India and Afghanistan Finally Get a Bilateral Series.
excerpt: The first-ever bilateral ODI series between the two nations begins in Dharamsala, with Kohli out, Rashid Khan in, and the 2027 World Cup on the horizon.
body:
They have played each other in World Cups and Asia Cups and the odd ICC event on neutral ground. But until Saturday, India and Afghanistan have never faced each other in a bilateral One Day International series. That changes when Shubman Gill leads India out at the HPCA Stadium in Dharamsala for the first of three ODIs — the start of a series that carries historical weight for Afghan cricket and serious selection implications for India ahead of the 2027 World Cup in South Africa.

## A Bilateral First, Decades in the Making

India and Afghanistan have met just four times in ODI cricket. India won three; the fourth, in the 2018 Asia Cup, ended in a tie. Every single encounter took place at a multi-team tournament on neutral or semi-neutral soil.

A full bilateral tour — three matches, Indian venues, Indian crowds — represents something altogether different for Afghanistan. It is a recognition of their standing as the seventh-ranked ODI side in the world, a team that no longer needs tournament scaffolding to justify a fixture against the game's richest board.

For Indian fans of Afghan cricket — and there are many, thanks to the IPL — this series is overdue. Rashid Khan has bowled for Gujarat Titans in front of 130,000 people at the Narendra Modi Stadium. Ibrahim Zadran has opened the batting at Wankhede. Mohammad Nabi has been a fixture in the league since its early expansions. These are not unfamiliar faces in Indian cricket. They are, in a very real sense, part of it.

## The Selection Puzzle: Who Bats at Number Three?

Virat Kohli's hamstring injury, sustained during the IPL 2026 final, has blown open the most debated position in Indian cricket. The BCCI named Yashasvi Jaiswal as his replacement in the squad, but the 24-year-old left-hander is primarily an opener — and with Rohit Sharma cleared fit and Shubman Gill captaining, both opening slots are occupied.

The leading candidate for the number three spot is Ishan Kishan, whose career resurrection over the past year reads like a film script. Stripped of his central contract in 2025 for skipping domestic cricket, Kishan led Jharkhand to the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy title, earned a T20 World Cup recall, and finished IPL 2026 as one of the most consistent performers in the tournament. Former India batter Aakash Chopra has called him "God's favourite child" and backed him to slot in at one-down.

The alternative is to push Gill down to three and give Jaiswal an opening berth alongside Rohit — a move that would give India a left-right combination at the top but disrupt a settled partnership. With the 2027 World Cup less than 18 months away, India's management will be looking for answers, not experiments.

## Rashid Khan's Record Against India

Rashid Khan has taken five wickets in three ODIs against India at an economy rate under six. More importantly, he has dismissed Indian batters in pressure moments — and he arrives in Dharamsala off the back of an impressive IPL 2026 season where his variations were as sharp as ever.

The leg-spinner will be partnered by AM Ghazanfar, whose mystery spin earned him a contract with Mumbai Indians, and the experienced Mohammad Nabi. India's middle order — likely Shreyas Iyer, KL Rahul, and Nitish Kumar Reddy in Hardik Pandya's absence — will face a spin challenge that they know well from the IPL but have rarely confronted in the national colours.

## The Dharamsala Factor

The HPCA Stadium, surrounded by the Dhauladhar mountain range, has hosted five World Cup matches and is known for pitches that offer carry and bounce — conditions closer to what both teams will encounter in South Africa next year than anything else on the Indian circuit.

Rain has been forecast for match day, which could reduce the contest and bring Duckworth-Lewis into play. If the weather clears, expect the toss to be crucial. Three of the five ODIs played here during the 2023 World Cup were won by the team batting first.

## What It Means for Afghan Cricket

For Afghanistan, this tour is about more than three matches. It is a statement of legitimacy. A bilateral series in India — with broadcast coverage on JioHotstar and Star Sports, with Indian crowds who know and respect Afghan players from the IPL — cements their position as a genuine force in the 50-over format.

Hashmatullah Shahidi's side know they are unlikely to win the series. But a competitive showing, particularly from their spin attack and the explosive opening pair of Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran, could shift how the cricket world perceives their 2027 World Cup credentials.

## Series Schedule

The first ODI is on Saturday, June 13, at 1:30 PM IST in Dharamsala (4 AM Eastern, 1 AM Pacific). The series moves to Lucknow on June 17 and concludes in Chennai on June 20. For NRIs, all three matches will be streamed on Willow TV and JioHotstar in the US.
